ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in square $ABCD$, $G$ is a point on diagonal $BD$, $GE \perp CD$, $GF \perp BC$, with $E$ and $F$ being the respective foot of the perpendiculars. Connect $EF$. Let $M$ and $N$ be the midpoints of $AB$ and $BG$ respectively. If $EF=5$, what is the length of $MN$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect AG and CG, \\
$\because$ In the square ABCD, $\angle$BCD$=90^\circ$, \\
$\because$ GE$\perp$CD, GF$\perp$BC, \\
$\therefore$ Quadrilateral CFGE is a rectangle, \\
$\therefore$ CG$=EF=5$, \\
$\because$ AB$=BC$, $\angle$ABD$=\angle$CBD$=45^\circ$, \\
$\because$ BG$=BG$, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ABG\cong \triangle CBG$ (SAS), \\
$\therefore$ AG$=CG=5$, \\
$\because$ M and N are respectively the midpoints of AB and BG, \\
$\therefore$ MN$=\frac{1}{2}AG=\boxed{2.5}$, \\
